questions.title: Steel ball inside a hollow cone — circular motion & angular speed

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: An arrow vertically downwards labelled ‘weight’, and an arrow perpendicular to the cone surface, pointing inwards and upwards, labelled ‘normal contact force’ (the two arrows must be in the correct directions and correctly labelled).

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer: The vertical component of the contact force equals the weight, so there is no resultant force vertically. The horizontal component of the contact force is the resultant force, and it acts towards the centre of the circle — this provides the centripetal force that keeps the ball moving in a circle.

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer:
For a conical-pendulum type of motion the acceleration is a = g tan 52°, and a = v²/r:
9.81 × tan 52° = v²/0.15
v² = 0.15 × 9.81 × tan 52° = 1.88 m² s⁻²
v = 1.4 m s⁻¹

parts.label: (d)
parts.answer:
v = rω, so ω = v/r = 1.4/0.15
= 9.3 rad s⁻¹
(Equivalently ω = √(g tan 52°/0.15) = 9.3 rad s⁻¹.)

parts.label: (e)
parts.answer: The resultant (centripetal) force — hence the acceleration — is unchanged, and a = v²/r, so v² is proportional to r. Therefore increasing the speed requires a larger radius, so the ball moves up the cone to a circle of larger radius.

questions.title: Gravitational potential of a planet & electric potential between plates

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: Sketch φ against x: a curve lying entirely in the negative-φ region for x between R and 4R, starting at (R, −φ) with a continuously decreasing magnitude and continuously decreasing gradient (concave up towards zero), and passing through (2R, −½φ) and (4R, −¼φ). The potential is φ = −GM/x, so it halves as x doubles.

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer: A geostationary satellite stays at the same point above the Earth, so its gravitational potential is constant: a horizontal straight line from t = 0 to t = 24 hours, starting at (0, −φ).

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer: The field between the plates is uniform, so the potential falls uniformly: a straight line with constant negative gradient from (0, V) to (d, 0), i.e. the potential decreases linearly from the positive plate to the negative plate.

questions.title: Thermal equilibrium, specific heat capacity & ideal gas

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.answer: P and Q are at the same temperature, so there is no net transfer of thermal energy between them.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.answer:
Energy is shared between P and Q, so Q = (mcΔT)P + (mcΔT)Q:
24 × 10³ = (0.54 × 390 × ΔT) + (0.37 × 910 × ΔT)
24 × 10³ = (210.6 + 336.7)ΔT = 547.3ΔT
ΔT = 44 K

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer:
Work done = pΔV = (1.6 × 10⁵) × (0.18 − 0.32)
= 1.6 × 10⁵ × (−0.14) = −2.2 × 10⁴ J
(The volume decreases, so work is done on the gas.)

questions.title: Piezoelectric crystal — simple harmonic motion & ultrasound

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.answer: Apply an alternating p.d. across the crystal. The p.d. causes the crystal to distort (change shape) at the frequency of the alternating p.d., so the surface vibrates — and conversely an oscillating crystal generates an alternating e.m.f., so it can be used to generate ultrasound.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.answer:
Z = ρc, so Zmuscle = 1100 × 1600 = 1.76 × 10⁶ and Zbone = 1900 × 4100 = 7.79 × 10⁶ kg m⁻² s⁻¹.
Intensity reflection coefficient = (Z₁ − Z₂)²/(Z₁ + Z₂)²
= (7.79 − 1.76)²/(7.79 + 1.76)² = 0.40 (40%)
so percentage transmitted = 60%

questions.title: Capacitor network — series/parallel & discharge through a resistor

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer:
For capacitors in series the charge is the same (Q = Q₁ = Q₂) and the p.d.s add (V = V₁ + V₂). Using V = Q/C:
Q/C = Q/C₁ + Q/C₂, which gives 1/C = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂.

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer:
Two equal capacitors C in series give C/2, so the total capacitance is C + C/2 = 3C/2.
The total capacitance equals the gradient of the Q–V graph = 400 × 10⁻⁶/6.0.
C = (2 × 400 × 10⁻⁶)/(3 × 6.0) = 44 μF

questions.title: Velocity selector — magnetic field, forces & ion paths

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: For undeviated motion the forces balance: FB = FE, so Bqu = qE. With E = V/d this gives Bqu = qV/d, so u = V/Bd.

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer: The expression u = V/Bd is independent of mass and charge, so the alpha particle also passes through undeviated at the same speed.

parts.label: (d)
parts.answer: There is no resultant force, so the magnetic force is upwards (equal and opposite to the downward electric force). The ions are positive, so the conventional current is from left to right. Using Fleming’s left-hand rule, the magnetic field is into the page.

parts.label: (e)
parts.answer: A curved path inside the plates with a consistent direction of curvature and no discontinuity at entry or in curvature, deflecting upwards (the magnetic force now exceeds the electric force, so the ions are deflected towards the top plate).

questions.title: Rod in a magnetic field — Faraday’s law & induced e.m.f.

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: The induced e.m.f. is (directly) proportional to the rate of change of (magnetic) flux (linkage).

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: The rod accelerates uniformly, so its velocity is proportional to time. Fig. 7.2 shows the e.m.f. is proportional to time, so E is proportional to v.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer: With v = at, the distance moved in time Δt is atΔt, so the area swept out is L × atΔt. The flux cut is ΔΦ = B × (area) = BLatΔt, and E = ΔΦ/Δt = BLat.

questions.title: Laser photons — energy, wavelength & radiation force

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: A photon is a quantum of energy of electromagnetic radiation.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer:
Number per unit time = power/energy per photon
= (1.0 × 10⁻²)/(1.96 × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹)
= 3.2 × 10¹⁶ s⁻¹

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.answer:
Force = rate of change of momentum, and for a photon p = E/c.
Half the photons are absorbed (momentum change p) and half are reflected (momentum change 2p), so the average momentum change per photon is (p + 2p)/2 = 3p/2.
F = (3/2) × (E/c) × (number per second)
= (3/2) × [(1.96 × 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹)/(3.00 × 10⁸)] × 3.2 × 10¹⁶
= 5.0 × 10⁻¹¹ N

questions.title: Polonium-193 decay — binding energy, half-life & PET

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.answer: Random — one cannot predict when a particular nucleus will decay (or which nucleus will decay next).

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.answer: Spontaneous — the decay is not affected by external or environmental factors.

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer: The time for the activity (or number of nuclei) to halve.

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer:
Energy released = total binding energy of products − total binding energy of the parent nucleus:
= (189 × 7.826) + (4 × 7.074) − (193 × 7.774)
= 1479.1 + 28.3 − 1500.4 = 7.03 eV

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.answer: The decay constant (the magnitude of the gradient of the ln(N/N₀)–t graph equals λ).

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.answer:
Decay constant λ = magnitude of gradient = 1.4/0.84.
Half-life = ln 2/λ = ln 2/(1.4/0.84)
= 0.42 ms

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.answer: The emitted positrons collide with electrons and annihilate, producing gamma-ray photons.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.answer: The half-life is long enough to allow the investigation to be carried out, but not so long that the patient is exposed to radiation unnecessarily.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.answer: The total power of radiation emitted (by the star).

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.answer: A standard candle has a known luminosity. Measure the radiant flux intensity F received at the Earth, then use F = L/(4πd²) to calculate the distance d to the galaxy.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer:
The two limbs of the Sun rotate in opposite directions, so the light from X and Y shows a rotational Doppler shift with Δλ = 656.2877 − 656.2831 nm. Using Δλ/λ = v/c and v = 2πR/T:
R = vT/2π = [3.00 × 10⁸ × (656.2877 − 656.2831)/656.2831] × (2.07 × 10⁶)/2π
= 6.93 × 10⁸ m

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer: Point Z is moving towards the Earth, so its light is blue-shifted: the observed wavelength from Z is less than the emitted wavelength.
